subject: ss-cardiology
title: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: genetics, outflow gradients, medical therapy and myectomy

steps.tx: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is defined by unexplained left ventricular wall thickness >= 15 mm in any myocardial segment, or >= 13 mm in individuals with a confirmed first-degree family history. Sarcomeric gene mutations account for up to 60% of familial cases, predominantly displaying autosomal dominant inheritance involving **MYH7** and **MYBPC3**.
steps.say: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is defined clinically by unexplained left ventricular hypertrophy with maximal wall thickness of 15 millimetres or greater, or 13 millimetres in the presence of a positive family history. Sarcomeric gene mutations account for up to 60 percent of familial cases, most commonly affecting MYH7 and MYBPC3.

steps.tx: Dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy results from systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve leaflets. Venturi forces and drag forces pull elongated leaflets toward the hypertrophied basal septum. A peak **outflow tract gradient** >= 30 mmHg defines obstruction, while a gradient >= 50 mmHg represents the threshold for invasive intervention.
steps.say: Dynamic left ventricular outflow tract obstruction in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is driven by systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve. Flow drag forces pull elongated leaflets toward the hypertrophied basal septum. A peak instantaneous gradient of 30 millimetres of mercury defines obstruction, whereas 50 defines the threshold for septal reduction.

steps.tx: The image shows marked thickening of the basal septum with the anterior mitral leaflet drawn toward the septum during systole, called **systolic anterior motion**. The narrowed passage accelerates flow and produces a dark **flow jet** through the **outflow tract**. Doppler confirms a peak gradient at or above 30 mmHg, the cutoff that defines obstruction and explains exertional symptoms and murmur.
steps.say: This scan shows obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. The basal septum is thick, the mitral leaflet moves forward in systole, and flow accelerates through the narrowed outflow tract. The measured peak gradient reaches the diagnostic cutoff for obstruction, so this anatomy explains dynamic symptoms.

vis.alt: Three chamber cardiac MRI shows asymmetric basal septal hypertrophy with systolic anterior motion of the mitral leaflet and a dark LVOT flow jet with Doppler gradient panels.

steps.tx: **First-line pharmacotherapy** for symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy consists of non-vasodilating beta-blockers titrated to a resting heart rate of 60 bpm. Nondihydropyridine calcium channel blockers such as verapamil serve as alternatives when beta-blockers are contraindicated. Both classes reduce inotropy, prolong diastole, and attenuate exercise-induced LVOT obstruction.
steps.say: First line medical therapy for symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy consists of nonvasodilating beta blockers titrated to a resting heart rate around 60 beats per minute. Verapamil represents an effective alternative. Both drug classes exert negative inotropic and chronotropic effects that attenuate dynamic outflow obstruction.

rows: Blunts adrenergic inotropy and heart rate
Slows AV nodal conduction and blunts contractility

steps.tx: **Mavacamten** represents a first-in-class cardiac myosin inhibitor that selectively and reversibly targets cardiac myosin ATPase. Inhibiting cross-bridge formation stabilizes myosin heads in the super-relaxed state, decreasing hypercontractility. In the EXPLORER-HCM and VALOR-HCM trials, mavacamten substantially reduced LVOT gradients, improved symptoms, and reduced the need for septal reduction therapy.
steps.say: Mavacamten is a first-in-class cardiac myosin inhibitor that reversibly inhibits cardiac myosin adenosine triphosphatase. Shifting myosin heads into a super relaxed state alleviates hypercontractility. In the EXPLORER-HCM trial, mavacamten markedly reduced outflow gradients and improved functional capacity in symptomatic obstructive patients.

left.title: Mavacamten Action
points: Direct, reversible allosteric inhibitor of beta-cardiac myosin; reduces excess actin-myosin cross-bridge formation.

right.title: Safety Requirement
points: Requires periodic echocardiographic LVEF surveillance; hold therapy if LVEF drops below 50% to prevent systolic dysfunction.

steps.tx: In patients with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, **dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers are contraindicated**, as well as nitrates, PDE-5 inhibitors, and digitalis. Peripheral vasodilation and volume depletion reduce left ventricular end-diastolic volume, while positive inotropes exaggerate hypercontractility, precipitating acute worsening of LVOT obstruction and hemodynamic collapse.
steps.say: In obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers, organic nitrates, and positive inotropic drugs like digoxin are strictly contraindicated. Peripheral vasodilation diminishes left ventricular cavity size, while inotropic stimulation exacerbates systolic anterior motion, drastically worsening outflow obstruction. Detailed mastery of these diagnostic thresholds and hemodynamic criteria is essential for clinical examination excellence.

left.title: Contraindicated Drugs
points: Amlodipine, nifedipine, nitroglycerin, isosorbide, digoxin, and aggressive loop diuretics.

right.title: Hemodynamic Consequence
points: Reduced afterload and smaller cavity volume precipitate catastrophic increase in LVOT obstruction and syncope.

steps.tx: Surgical **septal myectomy**, the Morrow procedure, remains the gold-standard septal reduction therapy for drug-refractory obstructive HCM with peak gradient >= 50 mmHg and severe symptoms. Alcohol septal ablation serves as an effective catheter-based alternative in high-surgical-risk patients possessing suitable septal perforator coronary artery anatomy.
steps.say: Surgical septal myectomy, known as the Morrow procedure, remains the gold standard septal reduction therapy for drug-refractory obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with peak gradients of 50 millimetres of mercury or greater. Alcohol septal ablation serves as an effective percutaneous alternative in patients with suitable coronary anatomy.

left.title: Surgical Myectomy
points: Transaortic resection of basal septal myocardium; addresses concomitant intrinsic mitral apparatus anomalies.

right.title: Alcohol Septal Ablation
points: Catheter-directed infusion of 96-98% ethanol into first septal perforator; produces targeted therapeutic basal infarction.

steps.tx: The cutaway shows the **Morrow procedure** result with a hollowed **resection trough** carved from the thick basal septum beneath the aortic valve. The widened channel is labeled relieved **outflow tract**, showing how removing muscle stops the mitral leaflet from blocking ejection. This surgical option suits drug refractory obstruction with high gradients and severe symptoms.
steps.say: This heart model shows surgery for thick heart muscle that blocks blood leaving the chamber. The surgeon has carved a trough from the bulky septum under the valve, opening a wide path for flow. Removing that shelf of muscle relieves the blockage when medicines alone cannot control symptoms.

vis.alt: Cutaway heart model shows a carved septal trough opening a wide outflow channel beneath the valve.

steps.tx: Major clinical risk factors for **sudden cardiac death** in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy include maximum LV wall thickness >= 30 mm, unexplained recent syncope, family history of premature HCM sudden death, apical aneurysm, LVEF < 50%, and extensive late gadolinium enhancement involving >= 15% of LV mass, guiding primary prevention ICD implantation.
steps.say: Major risk factors for sudden cardiac death in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy include massive left ventricular hypertrophy with maximal wall thickness of 30 millimetres or greater, unexplained recent syncope, family history of sudden death, apical aneurysm, and extensive late gadolinium enhancement involving at least 15 percent of myocardium.

rows: Premature sudden death in 1st degree relative

steps.tx: **Apical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy**, Yamaguchi syndrome, predominantly involves the LV apex with giant negative T waves >= 10 mm in precordial leads V2 to V5. Left ventriculography and cardiac MRI demonstrate pathognomonic ace-of-spades systolic cavity configuration. Apical aneurysms may develop, carrying substantial thromboembolic and ventricular arrhythmic risks.
steps.say: Apical hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, described by Yamaguchi, is characterized by selective hypertrophy of the left ventricular apex accompanied by giant negative T waves of ten millimetres or greater in precordial leads. Cardiac magnetic resonance demonstrates a characteristic ace of spades systolic cavity contour.

rows: Giant inverted T waves (>= 10 mm, V2-V5)
Obliteration of apical cavity in systole
